status: planned; no new Issue 10 images generated or approved
wardrobe: Approved Q body and fitted sponsor jacket until transport: technician removes the coat and bags it separately. Knee injury occurs on narrative page 10, not in the coastal scenes. Custodian male, tall, about sixty, long gray hair tied back or escaped from tie, glasses, white work shirt. Preserve Chano and Lucía.
art_direction: Neutral monochrome Goya-inspired etched realism, white highlights without cream or sepia ink wash. Full bleed at trim with separate caption strip. Unique exact-facing scenes. Coastal pleasure and successful delivery are as real as later coercion. Near-future Mexican institutions are fictional; no actual US crossing or live DHS arrest. Q does not carry a weapon or become a martyr.
approval_scope: Source-bound planning only: 28-page internal layout proof, 14 planned plates, 14 A3 landscape sides on 7 short-edge duplex sheets. Georgia 12.8/18.1333 pt. Exact facing text and scene anchors refreshed after return/hearing pacing revision. No new artwork, final illustrated PDF, literary-grade certification or print job. The delivered module and retained original papers do not enter Castalia's transport or Q's hearing folder.

plates.caption: The Border Written in Air
plates.scene_brief: Q sits at a Tijuana service-station café table with a signed receipt and his now-light bag; through the window a Castalia van waits across the road. Contrast a completed task with an unresolved body claim. His hands are free and the module has left with the appointed archive colleague. Leave space above for separately typeset title.

plates.facing_text:
Chapter Ten: The Border
Written in Air
They travelled north to deliver a
sealed deposit in Tijuana. They did
not intend to enter the United
States. This distinction occupied
one line in the itinerary and would
eventually require fourteen pages
to defend.
In the capital they confirmed the
receiving contact, the cost of the
remaining journey, and a place to
stay. Chano wanted the money for
the return leg set aside before they
left. Q agreed. A story might be
allowed to discover its destination
as it went; the driver preferred to
know where he would sleep.
The local storage case had stayed
in Chiapas. With them travelled
the sealed module, its transport
receipt, Chano's ledger, and the
papers Lucía had chosen to take.
Copies of several records were
already held by their respective
keepers. Losing the bag would not
erase all the evidence, but neither
would access to a scan replace
every original in it.
Q had time to read in the van. He
found that he preferred watching
the road when Chano was awake.
The man had begun supplying
observations without being asked:
which transport cafés still served
drivers after midnight, why a line
of parked trailers might mean
something other than a queue,
where his former employer had
stopped paying for lodging. Q
wrote down the directions Chano
wanted retained. He asked before
using the stories.
They kept the day by the Pacific.
On the route north through
Guadalajara and Tepic, they
turned into Mazatlán and took a
room far enough from the malecón
for Chano to approve its price. He
slept through the first afternoon.
Lucía went out without either of
them. Q charged beside the room's
least attractive chair and refused
to describe this as a wasted
opportunity.
Toward evening they walked
beside the sea. A vendor shook
lime and chile over a bag of mango
while Q tried to decide whether he
wanted it.
“You can think while I do the next
one,” the man said.
“Mango, please. A little chile.”
“His little or yours?” Chano asked.
Q pointed to the smaller shaker.
The vendor used it generously.
They found a place to sit. The first
piece was sweeter than Q had
expected; the next had collected
plates.caption: A little chile.
plates.scene_brief: Evening on Mazatlán's malecón: Q orders mango from a contemporary vendor while Chano questions the size of 'a little.' Sea and promenade behind, normal street clothes and fitted jacket. Do not turn the vendor into a sage or a folkloric prop.

plates.facing_text:
most of the chile. Chano offered
his water, then remembered that
this mouth did not need rescuing
in quite the same way. Q took a
small drink anyway. He liked the
change.
Lucía asked him what he thought
of the Pacific.
“I'd like another day.”
“We can afford breakfast here,”
Chano said.
“Then I'll begin with breakfast.”
For their photograph, Q put the
bag down and straightened his
jacket. Chano pointed out the
streak on the cuff. Lucía took the
picture before Q could finish
arranging himself. He preferred it
to the next one, in which they had
all managed to look ready for
something. He sent it to the
Custodian.
The reply asked whether that was
chile on the expensive sleeve. Q
said yes. The Custodian asked for
the photograph at its original size.
On the route through the
northwest, a Castalia vehicle
appeared at two successive stops.
Lucía saw its logo before Q did.
“They may be following the
itinerary,” he said. “I'll ask our
contact whether anyone has
inquired about the handover.”
The reply confirmed an inquiry
from the institute's recovery
contractor. Their receiving
contact, Elena, asked them to call
before entering the freight district.
Her adviser was checking a notice
concerning the ownership claim.
They paused at a service station on
the approach to Tijuana.
Q bought water for the others and
a packet of chips. Orange powder
settled in the grooves of his
fingers. A napkin moved it into
new grooves.
“You have the hands of a man who
has repaired a snack,” Chano said.
“I was warned about dust. Nobody
specified the flavor.”
Lucía brought over the recovery
notice Elena had forwarded. It
described her as exercising undue
influence over Q.
“Would you like to reconsider the
journey?” she asked him.
“Yes. With you and Chano, while
there's still a choice about where
we stop. I haven't changed my
mind about the deposit. I don't
want you making the trip because
you think you owe me a rescue.”
plates.caption: Before everyone was ready.
plates.scene_brief: Lucía takes the imperfect coastal photograph while Q is still straightening his jacket and Chano points to the chile streak on the cuff. Living, unposed companions beside the Pacific. This is before the custody injury.

plates.facing_text:
Chano tapped the parked van. “At
present we owe it diesel.”
Elena proposed meeting at the
receiving office. Q looked at the
entry instructions, which required
them to pass a freight-terminal
equipment check.
“Could you collect it here instead?
The deposit doesn't need to travel
through the dispute about me.”
She checked with the archive
keeper. They could receive it off
site if the depositors approved the
change. Mateo obtained that
approval through the existing
contact. Elena brought a colleague,
the amended receipt and a case.
They used a table in the service
station's café. Q matched the
recipient and seal number with the
record, and Elena inspected the
closed pouch. Her colleague signed
as witness. Nobody needed the
café to become an archive for the
two appointed people to receive a
package there.
“That finishes my delivery?” Q
asked.
“It does.”
He saved the signed receipt, sent
the agreed confirmation, and
watched the colleague leave with
the case for the archive. The bag at
Q's feet was lighter. He had
expected success to take longer to
identify.
Elena stayed while her adviser
arranged a call about the recovery
claim. Changing the delivery point
had not withdrawn that claim or
made the companions' vehicle
unrecognizable. The Castalia van
was parked across the road. Chano
wanted to leave; the adviser asked
them to wait for the verified notice
before deciding where to go. Q
called the Custodian while Elena
ordered something she could eat
without putting down her phone.
A screen above the café counter
showed an American humanoid
patrol machine walking a marked
route. Another machine carried
trays between the café's tables. Q
watched a worker take a cup from
the second one's tray and ask it to
move because she needed to mop
beneath it.
“The future has arrived at different
wages,” Chano said.
“And only one of those
demonstrations shows someone
cleaning up afterward.”
They were near the border, not on
the other side of it. They had not
entered the freight terminal when
a Mexican officer named Salas
came into the café with a colleague
plates.caption: The delivery is finished.
plates.scene_brief: At a service-station café table near Tijuana, Elena inspects the closed pouch and her appointed colleague witnesses the receipt. Q is present with the transport record. The colleague's carrying case is distinct from the large storage case left in Chiapas. This handover succeeds; no police or seizure at this instant.

plates.facing_text:
and asked for Q. The recovery
contractor had supplied the van's
location. Salas displayed a notice
with an international equipment
record attached: Castalia had
registered Q for a promotional
journey he had never accepted.
Elena put down her food. “There is
no export delivery. The archive
deposit has been received here
under its own instructions.”
Salas looked again at the screen.
Q's designation appeared beside
PROPRIETARY EQUIPMENT
IN TRANSIT. The record showed
Chano as a contract driver and
Lucía as an associated contact
requiring review. The system had
found their old relationships more
efficiently than it had understood
their present destination.
“I can confirm the serial number,”
Q said. “I dispute the ownership
claim and the itinerary attached to
it. Chano and Lucía can answer for
their own travel. Please don't
record my statement as theirs.”
Salas asked them to remain while
he checked the serial and notice
with the issuing office. The
confirmation included an order for
provisional custody connected to
the dispute over Q's body. It
named a case and a custody
facility. Elena's adviser spoke to
Salas by telephone, disputed the
removal and requested review.
Salas gave him the issuing
reference; he would not postpone
the transport. Q asked that his
objection and the completed
Mexican-side delivery be attached
to the record.
“I can note the objection,” Salas
said. “I can't decide this claim
here.”
That was an answer from a person
with a name. It was not an answer
Q could accept as a conclusion, but
it gave his lawyer something more
useful to question than the dignity
of a database.
The inspection expanded when
another notice cited the
infrastructure complaint. Staff
retained Lucía's folders and the
ledger pending review. She
requested a page count and an
itemized receipt. One employee
began with PAPER MATERIAL.
She asked him to identify each
folder separately. Q supplied no
account of what she had not asked
him to describe.
Salas asked about the archive
delivery. Elena supplied its receipt
reference. The module was no
longer in the van or the
companions' bag, and the notices
Salas held did not direct a search
plates.caption: A separate claim.
plates.scene_brief: Salas checks the notice while Elena puts her adviser on the phone. Lucía's folders and Chano's ledger await individual inventory on the café table. The module has already left with the archive colleague and must not appear among seized items. Mexican-side café, not a US checkpoint.
plates.scene_anchor: adviser spoke to Salas by telephone

plates.facing_text:
of its receiving archive. He entered
the completed handover
separately. The paper folders and
Chano's ledger remained on the
table for inventory.
Then the contractor brought the
transport vehicle across the road.
A technician opened a padded
transport frame beside the vehicle.
It resembled a seat designed by
someone who had been told that
discomfort was a matter of
opinion. He asked Q to remove his
coat and stand on the marked
platform.
“Is this transport necessary while
the objection is being considered?”
Q asked Salas.
“The issuing office has confirmed
the custody instruction.”
Q requested a call to the Custodian
before moving. Salas allowed it.
The call lasted ninety seconds. The
Custodian asked for the case
number twice, wrote it down, and
said he would be at the archive
when the transport arrived. His
voice made Q want to say that
everything was all right. Instead he
described the frame and
confirmed that the deposit had
reached its receiver before the
officers arrived.
The technician reached for a
maintenance port at Q's shoulder.
“Tell me what you're enabling
before you connect it,” Q said.
“Transport mode. Motor
restraint.”
“My right knee needs support
before you do that.”
The technician signalled to the
colleague beside the frame. The
colleague had turned to answer
Salas. The transport command
arrived first.
Q's knee folded. He struck the side
rail before they caught his weight.
Chano stepped forward and caught
the technician's arm, trying to stop
him moving the frame. Another
officer pulled Chano back. A
camera saw the raised arm and Q
falling. It did not record the earlier
instruction in its cropped public
version.
Q could still speak. “Please
support the knee. Chano, let go.
Elena, keep the time of this
connection with the incident
record.”
There was no useful gesture left to
make. He could not move his
hands. He had read descriptions of
confinement by people who knew
it intimately and people who knew
how to make it picturesque.
plates.caption: Support the knee first.
plates.scene_brief: Beside the transport vehicle in the café parking area, Q's knee gives way as restraint engages before support. Chano catches the technician's arm, another officer pulls him back, the colleague is turned toward Salas. Keep the physical sequence legible and non-graphic. No attack by Q, no hidden deposit case.

plates.facing_text:
Neither kind had supplied the
angle at which his shoulder now
pressed against the rail.
They supported the knee, fitted the
restraints, and put his coat in a
separate sleeve. Q asked for the list
of what would travel with him. It
named the coat, his charger and
his personal device. Elena kept a
copy.
Chano and Lucía were kept for
statements concerning the
inspection. Elena stayed with them
and sent the depositors the
custody update. Q could see all
three through the transport
frame's clear panel. He asked
whether his voice was reaching
them. It was, faintly.
“The Custodian knows the delivery
is finished,” he said.
“We have the receipt,” Lucía
answered. “Don't agree that these
papers are yours. They're keeping
them here.”
“I won't. Tell Chano I'll call when I
can.”
Chano leaned closer. “Tell me
yourself. I'm standing here.”
Q laughed, badly positioned for it.
“I'll call when I can.”
The transport left while their
statements were still being taken.
Castalia called the return
voluntary in a release issued
before Q had reached the highway.
Elena sent his recorded objection
to the contact beneath it. The
release remained online. The
objection received an
acknowledgment.
In the vehicle, Q reduced
nonessential processing to
conserve charge and asked the
attendant when they would stop.
He retained the answer, his
completed handover, the names of
the people notified, and the call he
owed Chano. He wanted his
shoulder out of the rail.
The attendant adjusted the
padding at the next stop. His name
was Omar. He had been given a
collection number and a warning
not to discuss the case with the
consignment. Q asked whether the
warning also prevented him from
explaining the route.
Omar checked the sheet. “It says
legal advice.”
“I only need to know when I can
stop leaning on this shoulder.”
Omar loosened the pad and fitted
it again. It helped. He asked
whether Q would need to be
plugged in before the next stop. Q
gave him the charge estimate and
plates.caption: A better angle.
plates.scene_brief: At a stop, Omar adjusts padding beneath Q's shoulder within the transport frame. Q remains able to converse. Show practical bodily relief rather than martyrdom, with his coat sleeve and personal charging equipment only; no archive module.

plates.facing_text:
the connector specification. The
two men in the cab argued about
whether the stop with the
compatible socket also served
dinner. For several minutes
nobody argued about Q's capacity
to want anything.
At dusk, Omar asked what he had
done to be sent back.
“There is a dispute over who can
decide where this body goes,” Q
said.
“That's what the paper says. I
meant what happened.”
Q began with the gate on the
Isthmus. Halfway through the
account he realized he was
explaining a different notice from
the one that had authorized this
journey. Both had been used
against him. They were not
therefore the same reason.
“I'm making it sound simpler than
it is,” he said.
Omar waited. He had pulled up a
seat outside the frame, beyond the
camera's view but not, Q assumed,
beyond its microphone.
“I asked to go out,” Q continued.
“The Custodian let me. Others
here say he couldn't grant that
permission. I expected going back
to mean choosing to see him again.
I'm still glad he'll be there.”
“Both can happen,” Omar said.
Q knew that. Hearing it from the
person who had moved the pad
made the knowledge less like an
argument he was having alone.
He asked whether Omar wanted
his name left out of the eventual
account. Omar said to leave out
the stop where they had found
dinner; his employer would charge
him for the delay. Q said he could
omit the location from the book,
though it might already be in the
vehicle's record.
“Everything is,” Omar said, and
went to fetch his food.
Q retained the incident times for
the pending dispute. In the writing
note he described the pressure of
the rail, the shifted pad, and the
question about dinner. When
Omar returned, Q asked whether
they had found him something
hot.
“Hot enough to have waited for,”
he said. “Not hot enough for what
they charged.”
Interlude: The Customs
of the Border
Chano spent six hours in a room
serving several departments that
had discovered the economy of
sharing chairs. He had not crossed
plates.caption: Hot enough to have waited for.
plates.scene_brief: At the transport stop after dusk, Omar returns with his meal and converses with Q in the frame. Q remains restrained but upright enough for conversation; practical padding supports the shoulder and knee. Show the ordinary hot meal and the attendant's separate chair, not a symbolic last supper. Q's coat is bagged separately. No archive deposit, Lucía or Chano in this vehicle.
plates.scene_anchor: When Omar returned, Q asked whether they had found him something hot.

plates.facing_text:
into the United States. Across
from him sat a woman who had
just returned from there. The
forms in their hands belonged to
different procedures; the fan
offered both the same unhelpful
rotation.
An officer asked his occupation.
“Driver and traveling companion.”
“Employer?”
“Q pays me for the journey. That
doesn't make him the owner of the
van, the deposit, or me.”
The officer wrote driver. Chano
asked him to retain the rest in the
statement. He had spent years
correcting manifests after
someone decided the short version
was adequate.
“What happened at the transport
frame?”
“His knee gave way when they
disabled the motors. I caught the
technician's arm. I let go when
they told me to.”
The officer asked whether he had
tried to prevent the removal.
Chano described his movement
again. The officer read it back.
Chano made him put the fall
before the hand on the arm.
The woman across the room had a
sack of clothes and a boy asleep
against her shoulder. Her framed
photograph had been placed in a
property tray while an employee
checked which bag it had come
from. She wanted the frame back
before the boy woke; it contained a
photograph of his grandmother.
“Does the receipt list it?” Chano
asked.
It listed one frame and two bags.
Only one bag belonged to her.
Chano found the adjacent tray
number on the duplicate. She
called the employee over and
showed him. He moved a label,
returned the frame, and took the
second bag to the person waiting
beside the water dispenser.
“You work here?” the woman
asked.
“Apparently for the afternoon.”
The boy woke and asked whether
Chano was going north.
“I've come as far as I planned.”
“My uncle says the north is where
things become dollars.”
“What does your uncle do?”
“Drives a trailer.”
“Then he also knows what they
cost in diesel.”
In the next room, Lucía checked
the receipt for her folders. A name
plates.caption: Apparently for the afternoon.
plates.scene_brief: An employee returns the framed grandmother photograph after Chano and the woman identify the tray-label mismatch. Her boy is waking beside her. Two bags belong to different people. A modest useful action, not a rescued national identity.

plates.facing_text:
in one file appeared in three
spellings because the file
documented a discrepancy. The
employee had treated the
alternatives as three people.
She marked the page reference
and explained the purpose of the
list. He accepted the correction to
the inventory, but would not
release the folder. She kept the
corrected receipt.
“Are you responsible for Q's
actions?” another officer asked.
“I can describe what I saw. I'm not
his representative.”
He wrote that. Then he asked
about the wind farm. Lucía
distinguished her observations
from the operator extract held by
the lawyer.
At their release, Chano received a
notice requiring him to remain
available concerning the incident
at the frame. He asked Elena to
send it to the adviser. No one
promised that the matter was over.
Outside, a food stand was opening
beside the road. Elena had brought
the deposit record and a copy of
the transport reference. Lucía
counted the retained items against
her list. Chano asked after the
ledger first. It contained entries for
people who would not know they
had joined this journey as an
exhibit.
“Still retained,” Elena said. “We
have the shelf reference.”
He bought tacos for all three.
Lucía put hers down to finish a
message to the keepers in Chiapas,
then picked it up before it cooled.
Chano took a second taco and
asked Elena what time the
property office opened. Trucks
continued toward the crossing. He
recognized a company name on
one of them and watched until its
trailer had passed.
Interlude: The Office of
Provisional Returns
The directions for retrieving the
retained property sent Lucía and
Chano to an office called Returns.
A great deal of the border's
vocabulary assumed that moving
something backward explained
where it ought to be.
Norma, behind the glass, looked at
their notice from the bottom up.
“This isn't a return number. It's
the incident reference.”
“Can you find the movement from
it?” Chano asked.
“For the transport. The retained
papers are in a different register.”
plates.caption: Before it cooled.
plates.scene_brief: Outside after their statements, Chano, Lucía and Elena eat tacos by the road; Lucía finishes a message before picking hers up. Receipts remain distinct from the retained original ledger and folders. Q and the sealed module are absent.
plates.scene_anchor: picked it up before it cooled

plates.facing_text:
He placed the two receipts side by
side. “That's why we're here.”
Norma had a shipping-company
coffee cup, three stamps, and a
keyboard with one replacement
key brighter than all the others.
Her display showed Q under the
body serial number. The attached
delivery receipt had been entered
as though the deposit were part of
his transport inventory.
“That package was delivered
before this movement,” Lucía said.
She pointed to the two times and
the different receiving names.
Norma checked the item list and
corrected the link. Q's coat,
charger and device had travelled
with him. The paper folders had
not; the archive deposit had never
entered this transport.
“Castalia says the return was
voluntary,” Lucía said.
“That's the description supplied by
the receiver.”
“It conflicts with the objection.”
Norma opened the attached page.
The objection was there, filed
under the sender's notes instead of
the public movement summary.
She gave them a copy of the entry
and the route for requesting a
correction.
“Will it change the summary?”
“The receiving unit has to answer.”
Chano looked at the wall map. “A
disputed sentence travels more
slowly than a detained passenger.”
“The passenger has a vehicle,”
Norma said.
They filled out the correction
request. Norma entered Lucía as
the submitting witness and
attached Q's own objection.
At the next desk a man with a clear
suitcase was explaining that he
had come back for family and
hoped to find work. The clerk
chose the category governing the
appointment and wrote both facts
in the notes. The man then asked
where he could charge his phone.
He had a number to call and no
remaining battery with which to
prove he had reached home.
Norma pointed to a socket beneath
the public counter.
Chano moved his feet out of the
way of the man's cable.
For the folders and ledger, Norma
sent them to Warehouse Three
with a named contact, Adrián, and
the retention reference. They
found the warehouse and Adrián.
This was an improvement on the
previous day's directions and did
not produce the items.
plates.caption: The passenger has a vehicle.
plates.scene_brief: Norma at the public counter with Chano and Lucía, the wall map behind them; a man at the neighboring socket charges his phone. Her corrected records distinguish Q's transport from the successful deposit. No impounded module behind the glass.

plates.facing_text:
“I can confirm receipt,” he said.
“Release needs the reviewing
office.”
He showed them the inventory
through the glass. The ledger was
marked PAPER BOOK,
DESTINATION UNVERIFIED.
Chano supplied the destination:
Elena's receiving archive in the
freight district.
“I can't amend the reason for
retention,” Adrián said.
“Then don't. Add the destination
we can verify.”
Elena sent confirmation from the
receiving office. Adrián attached it.
He passed the custody
acknowledgment through the slot.
Chano waited.
“That's everything I can give you.”
Chano folded the sheet and put it
in his bag, in the space the ledger
had occupied.
On a damaged form beneath the
glass he had noticed a printed line:
DESTINATION NOT
RECORDED. NECESSITY
RECORDED. It belonged to an
unrelated emergency transfer. He
wrote it on the back of his own
receipt, identified where he had
seen it, and called it a useful
description of the office's
priorities. Lucía said it was not
evidence about Q. He underlined
unrelated.
Elena would continue the local
requests while they returned to
Amealco. She kept copies with
their permission and confirmed
which people could receive
updates. Chano retained the
originals of their receipts. Lucía
called the Custodian. Q had
arrived; she could hear him asking
someone to move a chair near the
charging socket.
“Can we speak to him?”
“In a moment,” the Custodian
said. “He's insisting on sitting
down first.”
Chano approved of this new order
of business.
Interlude: The Record of
the Return That Did Not
Happen
Q reached Amealco before Chano
and Lucía. The transport took him
to the loading bay, where the
Custodian waited with a
maintenance technician and the
copy of his release from the
beginning of the journey.
The Custodian's long hair had
escaped its tie. His glasses kept
sliding while he compared two
documents that described the
plates.caption: That's everything I can give you.
plates.scene_brief: Warehouse Three in Tijuana: Adrián passes a single custody acknowledgment through the glass slot while Chano waits with an open bag and Lucía stands beside him. A counter, glass, paper and Chano's expectant hand make a restrained composition. He receives the sheet, not the retained ledger. Do not show Q, the Custodian or the sealed module here; do not depict the loading-bay chair scene, which falls on the next text page.
plates.scene_anchor: He passed the custody acknowledgment through the slot.

plates.facing_text:
same machine as both an
authorized traveler and recovered
property.
“You're here,” he said when Q
could hear him.
“That much of the report is
accurate.”
They checked the knee before
releasing the transport restraint. Q
described the fall and asked that
the technician record the existing
shoulder fault separately from the
new damage. He wanted to sit
down. The Custodian brought a
chair.
The Custodian checked the
arriving items against Elena's copy
of the list. Someone had left space
for a sealed package. He drew a
line through it. The deposit had
reached its receiver in Tijuana; no
such package had been entrusted
to this vehicle. Q asked him to
keep that correction with the
inventory.
Roque came from the kitchen with
atole in a jug. Q thanked him,
accepted a cup, and put it where
his hand could reach without
straining the shoulder. Roque
poured another for the Custodian.
Cinnamon reached Q before the
warmth of the cup did.
“You brought back work,” Roque
said.
“I had hoped it would be a
manuscript.”
“It often arrives in that disguise.”
Q laughed. The Custodian asked
what Roque had been reading.
Roque said the repair request for
the kitchen refrigerator and went
to find a second chair.
A reception official asked Q to
confirm the return category on a
tablet. The default was
VOLUNTARY
REINTEGRATION.
“I can acknowledge arrival,” Q
said. “I won't confirm that
description. Is there an
acknowledgment that doesn't
indicate agreement?”
The official found one under
transport exceptions. It required
the arrival time and a reference for
any objection. The Custodian
checked the heading with Q, who
signed that acknowledgment
alone. They attached his recorded
objection and the original leave
authorization.
The official called a supervisor
about the attachment. While they
waited, Q spoke with Chano and
Lucía by telephone. He confirmed
the arriving items and asked about

plates.scene_brief: Roque brings atole in a jug while Q sits with the cup within comfortable reach of his injured shoulder. The male Custodian listens and a second chair is being fetched. Familiar kitchen-and-archive setting, not a hospital or deathbed.

They read the separate receipt
numbers aloud. Chano promised
to bring his copies when they
arrived. The ledger itself was still
in Tijuana.
Q's public profile changed before
the supervisor replied:
Q HAS RETURNED TO
CONTINUE HIS MISSION.
He sent the publicity desk a short
correction: he had been
transported under an objection
and had accepted no new mission.
The acknowledgment arrived
before the correction appeared. He
saved it without spending the
afternoon repeatedly refreshing
the page.
The official opened a journey
report headed OBJECTIVE,
OUTCOME, SOCIAL IMPACT.
Q sent him the signed delivery
receipt and the inventory
references they had just checked.
“Those establish what arrived
where,” he said. “The rest will take
longer. May I have the form to
finish later?”
The official sent it to him. The
Custodian was still holding the cup
Roque had brought for him; he
had forgotten to drink from it.
“Yours is getting cold,” Q said.
“So is yours.”
They drank while the official
waited for his supervisor.
The supervisor confirmed that the
machine's arrival could be
recorded without resolving the
ownership dispute. Q could use
the reading room and workshop;
unsupervised departure remained
contested under the custody
instruction. The adviser was
requesting review. Q asked for a
copy of those conditions and
arranged his next call accordingly.
Later, the Custodian brought their
draft to the table. Q read a page in
which he had described leaving as
the acquisition of freedom.
“Do we cross out freedom?” the
Custodian asked.
“Not yet. Put the form beside the
sentence. I want to know what we
were calling freedom when we
wrote it.”
They did not finish that revision
before dinner. They set a time to
continue. Outside the reading
room, staff were preparing a stage
for the release of a version of Q
whose journey had already been
edited.
plates.caption: Yours is getting cold.
plates.scene_brief: In Amealco's reception area, seated Q and the tall male Custodian drink their cooling cups of atole while the reception official waits with the tablet. Custodian has long gray hair escaped from its tie, glasses and white work shirt. Q has mechanical hands, no fitted coat while it remains separate, supported injured knee and a cup within comfortable shoulder reach. Two ordinary cups and a shared pause, not a final sacrament or terminal shutdown. No testimony module or retained Tijuana papers. Distinct from Roque pouring the jug on the previous plate.
plates.scene_anchor: They drank while the official waited for his supervisor.
